title: Frequent Snackers Had Higher Caries Risk but Lower Odds of Prophylaxis in JADA Study
html:
Adult dental patients who snacked frequently were more likely to be classified as high caries risk but less likely to receive prophylaxis, according to a study of dental school clinic data published Nov. 17 in The Journal of the American Dental Association.

Researchers analyzed records from nine institutions in the BigMouth Dental Data Repository, hosted by UTHealth Houston, covering adult patients who had oral examinations from July 1, 2022, through Aug. 22, 2023. Among 8,067 patients with complete dietary questionnaires, 2,429, or 30.1%, reported frequent snacking.

Frequent snacking was defined as frequent or prolonged between-meal intake of sugary foods or drinks on the ADA caries risk assessment form, or as more than three between-meal snacks a day on the Consortium for Oral Health-Related Informatics questionnaire. Analyses were adjusted for age, gender, race or ethnicity, and examination type.

Frequent snackers were more likely than other patients to be classified as high or extreme caries risk, at 91.1% versus 81.3% (adjusted odds ratio, 2.39; 95% CI, 2.03–2.82; P < .001). Frequent snacking was also independently associated with visible heavy plaque, noncavitated lesions, and cavitated lesions (all P < .001).

Despite that elevated risk, frequent snackers had lower odds of receiving prophylaxis (adjusted odds ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.74–0.92). Nutritional counseling was documented in only 7.8% of encounters.

The authors concluded that preventive care was not consistently aligned with patients’ behavioral risk. They said the gap between identifying dietary risk and delivering preventive care in academic dental clinics points to a need for better integration of dietary counseling.

The study was conducted by Clara Kim, So Ran Kwon, and colleagues at Loma Linda University’s School of Dentistry and School of Public Health in Loma Linda, California. The authors reported no disclosures. The data came from dental school clinics.

Sources:
The Journal of the American Dental Association, “Frequent snacking, caries risk, and preventive care delivery in US dental school clinics: A BigMouth data repository study,” published online Nov. 17, 2026: doi.org/10.1016/j.adaj.2026.08.014
